title: Randomness can be certified in energy-constrained semi-device-independent scenarios
authors: Shashank Kumar Ranu, Lewis Wooltorton, Alastair A. Abbott, Omar Fawzi
abstract: The prepare-and-measure framework based on energy constraints offers a practical middle ground between fully device-dependent and device-independent quantum cryptography. The only assumption on an otherwise uncharacterized prepare-and-measure device is that the energy of the prepared states is bounded. Existing security analyses of this framework assume that the preparation and measurement devices share at most classical correlations, and under this assumption certified lower bounds on the extractable randomness have been established. Recent work has shown that an adversary who pre-distributes entanglement between the devices can mount attacks that are strictly more powerful than those available when the devices share only classical correlations, reducing the extractable randomness below the previously certified rates. This leaves open the fundamental question of whether randomness can be certified at all in this scenario.   We address this open question by constructing semidefinite programming relaxations of the guessing probability by adapting the Navascués-Pironio-Acín hierarchy to the energy-constrained setting where shared entanglement between the devices is permitted. Our relaxations yield certified lower bounds on the extractable randomness without enforcing any restrictions on the dimensions of the quantum state shared between the preparation and measurement devices. We show that these certified lower bounds are strictly positive for a range of energy values, thereby answering the open question affirmatively: certified randomness generation is theoretically possible in the energy-constrained SDI framework even in the presence of a fully quantum adversary.
summary: This paper establishes the theoretical possibility of generating certified randomness in energy-constrained semi-device-independent quantum cryptography. By adapting the NPA hierarchy to incorporate energy bounds, the authors derive SDP relaxations that provide lower bounds on the min-entropy even when the adversary has full quantum access. This resolves a long-standing open question in the field.
main_problem: To determine if certified randomness can be generated in energy-constrained semi-device-independent (SDI) quantum cryptography scenarios, especially when the adversary can share quantum entanglement.
main_result: The authors affirmatively answer the open question, proving that certified randomness generation is theoretically possible even against a fully quantum adversary, yielding positive lower bounds on the min-entropy.
method: They adapt the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy to construct semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations of the guessing probability, allowing for dimension-independent security proofs.
model_or_system: The model is a prepare-and-measure (PM) framework for quantum random number generation, constrained by a finite energy bound ($\omega$) on the prepared states.
key_observables: The primary observables are the extractable min-entropy ($H_{\min}$) and the correlator difference ($I_{	ext{corr}}$), which quantify the security and randomness rate.
important_parameters: The energy parameter ($\omega$) is crucial, as the certified rate remains positive for a range of small energy values.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is the energy constraint on the prepared states. The analysis is strongest when assuming the adversary can share full quantum entanglement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy-constrained PM scenario, showing the certified $H_{\min}$ vs. $\omega$ for different dimension assumptions, and demonstrating the robustness of $H_{\min}$ when the observed correlator is reduced.
paper_structure: The paper develops the SDP relaxation by adapting the NPA hierarchy to the energy-constrained setting, deriving structural constraints on the POVM elements, and finally solving the optimization problem to yield the certified lower bound on randomness.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, device-independent security guarantees for quantum random number generation under realistic physical constraints (energy), which is highly relevant for quantum optics and quantum information hardware.

FIG. 2: Certified min-entropy Hmin as a function of the energy parameter ω without the dimension assumption (red curve). The blue curve shows the certified lower bound in the separable (no shared entanglement) scenario [17]. The orange curve shows the upper bound obtained via the seesaw method in the entangled scenario with dim(HS) = dim(HM) = 2 [22, 23]. The green curve shows our certified lower bound with dim(HS) = 2 and dim(HM) unbounded.
FIG. 3: Certified lower bounds on Hmin as a function of the energy parameter ω for source dimensions dim(HS) = 2 (orange) and dim(HS) = 3 (blue).

Figure 4 shows the certified min-entropy as a function of Iexp corr at ω = 0.05 and ω = 0.1. In both cases Hmin decreases monotonically as the observed correlator is reduced and vanishes at a value strictly below the ideal one. For ω = 0.05, the bound remains positive down to Iexp corr ≈0.50, compared with the ideal value of ≈0.87. Similarly, for ω = 0.1, the ideal correlator value is 1.2, and positive min-entropy is certified above approximately 0.948, corresponding to about 79% of the ideal value. Operating at low energy is therefore doubly advantageous, yielding both a higher certified rate and greater robustness to imperfections in the observed statistics.

FIG. 4: Certified min-entropy Hmin from the dimension-independent relaxation as a function of the observed correlator Iexp corr at (a) ω = 0.05 and (b) ω = 0.1. The ideal correlator values are approximately 0.87 and 1.2, respectively, attained at the right-hand end of each curve.
